claims.text: The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy is equiatomic.
The initial alloy is as-cast and homogenized.
Homogenization ensures a uniform distribution of lattice distortions.
Severe local lattice distortions caused by atomic-size mismatch contribute to the elevated-temperature mechanical responses of HfNbTaTiZr.
High-temperature dynamic recovery contributes to the elevated-temperature mechanical responses by modifying dislocation pinning and microstructural rigidity.
The proposed annealing treatment will produce partial recovery and reduce dislocation density without changing the overall phase structure.
The proposed annealing treatment will slightly relax local lattice distortions.
Elevated temperature increases atomic mobility in HfNbTaTiZr.
Increased atomic mobility triggers recovery that partially relaxes severe local lattice distortions.
Relaxation of local lattice distortions reduces the effectiveness of dislocation pinning.
Dislocation pinning enhances yield strength and elastic modulus.
Relaxation of local lattice distortions alters phonon scattering and thereby influences thermal expansion.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, annealed samples will have lower yield strength at the high-temperature end of the test range.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, annealed samples will have a lower elastic modulus at the high-temperature end because of enhanced dislocation mobility.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, annealed samples will have a lower thermal-expansion coefficient below the temperature at which dynamic recovery becomes dominant.
As temperature approaches 1200°C, the annealed samples will show increased plasticity and altered thermal-expansion behavior.
The hypothesized behavior is limited to 600–1200°C and strain rates below 10^-3 s^-1.
Outside the specified regime, oxidation or grain-boundary diffusion may become significant.
Low strain rates below 10^-3 s^-1 minimize rate effects.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as both as-cast and homogenized, whereas the baseline is described as untreated and as-cast. It is unclear whether the baseline underwent homogenization.

The intervention is a pre-test annealing treatment, but the resulting process is repeatedly called dynamic recovery. The hypothesis does not distinguish static recovery during annealing from dynamic recovery during mechanical loading.
